subject: Control articulation, ISO timelines, and FedRAMP evidence windows — sync with Acme
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@acme-enterprises.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Control articulation, ISO timelines, and FedRAMP evidence windows — sync with Acme

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for taking time today. Per our call, I wanted to start a concise thread we can use to lock down three things from Acme's side before we finalize our certification roadmap:

1) The specific artifact windows you need for FedRAMP low readiness validation (e.g., last 12 months vs. 90 days for logging samples).
2) Which ISO 27001 control narratives you want aligned to (Annex A mappings) versus a high-level SOC 2 mapping we can provide.
3) Any audit timing constraints where we should stage evidence pulls (blackout windows, audit teams availability).

Attached is the compliance roadmap draft we referenced — it has our proposed gate dates and a preliminary artifact request matrix. Can you confirm: 1) whether Acme requires live system log exports or redacted extracts, and 2) if you have a preferred evidence sampling cadence (e.g., one-week snapshot, monthly rolling window)?

Proposed next step: share the matrix with your security team, populate the columns for artifacts you require, and we'll update the control owners on our side. If easier, loop in Patrick and we can do a 30-minute intake to avoid back-and-forth.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: compliance-roadmap-draft.pdf (PDF, 420KB); artifact-request-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@acme-enterprises.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Cc: security@acme-enterprises.com, Patrick Doyle <patrick.doyle@ciso-consulting.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Control articulation, ISO timelines, and FedRAMP evidence windows — sync with Acme

Naomi —

Appreciate the clear summary. Quick answers from Acme security:

- For FedRAMP low pathing, we typically ask for 12 months of system and access logs, but we accept a 90-day rolling window for higher-frequency artifacts (e.g., auth events) if the last 12 months are archived and can be produced on investigator request.
- ISO 27001: we want mappings to Annex A controls for the controls in scope (A.9, A.12, A.14 are most important for our environment). A SOC 2 crosswalk is helpful for our procurement team but the auditor will focus on ISO narratives.
- Audit timing: our external assessor has a week-long evidence intake window locked for 2026-06-07 through 2026-06-11; if Redwood can commit to a dedicated pull window in that period that reduces risk for scheduling.

We'll look at the matrix and add comments. CC'd our security ops alias and Patrick who can help if we need to formalize sample sizes.

—Sarah Lim
Director, Security Assurance
Acme Enterprises

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Control articulation, ISO timelines, and FedRAMP evidence windows — sync with Acme

Thanks Sarah — helpful. A couple follow-ups so we can action:

- We'll prepare two flavors of log export guidance: a) redacted extracts suitable for public review and b) full-system exports for assessor use under an NDA. Which do you prefer as the default for the June window?
- For ISO Annex A mapping: we'll send a short narrative per control (A.9, A.12, A.14) and a pointer to our evidence. Expect that as a first pass by Friday (2026-01-16).
- Regarding sample sizes: we propose a 7-day snapshot for live testing during the June intake and then an archived 12-month export for any retrospective requests. If Patrick has a differing approach, please advise.

I'm attaching a populated artifact-request-matrix with our initial assumptions and where we need Acme to confirm required retention/level-of-detail. If acme security can mark required level (redacted vs full), we'll lock the schedule and assign control owners internally.

Naomi

Attachments: artifact-request-matrix.xlsx (v0.2)
